call_sites: 2 consumers read each source's source_candidates list: map_signals (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:1036, updated to cand['path']) and _prepare_section_context (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:1225, still cand.hit.path — unrepointed).

findings.text: CONFIRMED correctness: _prepare_section_context (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:1225-1233) was not repointed to the new source_candidates shape. gather_ids_context now stores list[dict] (read_candidates), but this consumer still reads cand.hit.path / cand.hit.score, the shape of the removed retrieve_candidates Candidate. It is the path the live map worker takes (workers.py:679 -> _prepare_section_context; amap_signals mapping.py:1123 also calls it). Reproduction at head 5370d74d, monkeypatching fetch_imas_fields/fetch_imas_subtree/fetch_source_code_refs and passing a context whose source_candidates came from read_candidates: `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'hit'`. Fix: read cand['path'] / cand.get('retrieval_score') / cand.get('documentation') as map_signals already does, and add a test that drives _prepare_section_context with populated source_candidates.

follow-on: select_candidates (imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:636) partially marks before it refuses. Its statement runs FOREACH (rel IN found | SET rel.route = true) and then sets candidate_route via CASE, and only after the query returns does the Python code raise CandidateWriteError when matched < len(chosen), followed by CandidateWriteError before any rollback (GraphClient.query uses an auto-committing session, client.py:1004). So on refusal the matched edges keep route=true while candidate_route is null. The docstring says the route is left null so the source is re-judged, and re-judgment rewrites all edges, so the state is transient — but a caller that swallows the error would leave a source with partial selected edges and a null route. Low severity; no production caller exists yet (the next node wires select_candidates).

follow-on (accepted): docs/evidence/fragments/mapping-candidate-selection/map-context-reads-candidates.html is outside the node's plan write paths for map-context-reads-candidates; it is a landing-evidence artifact declared in the node's orientation_write_paths, not a code change.

item_verdicts.manifest: present and self-consistent at head (status complete; commit 5370d74db; gate.log 530 passed EXIT=0; negative_control.log 1 failed EXIT=1; blockers none; the seven retry_failures are attributed to a fixture path mismatch in test_discover_map). Its baseline_suite and after_suite arms are both empty, so this review derived them itself.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the delta touches imas_codex/ids/{graph_ops,mapping,tools,workers}.py, imas_codex/cli/discover/__init__.py, tests/ids/{test_candidate_persistence,test_candidates}.py, tests/cli/test_discover_map.py, tests/tools/test_dd_version_filtering.py and the evidence fragment; all but the fragment are inside the node's plan write paths.

justifications.durability: The work is committed (single commit 5370d74db with a mechanism-stated body), the model change is defined once in graph_ops.py and reused, and dead capability is removed rather than shadowed (count_sources_by_mapping_status and the imas arm deleted, no parallel paths left). The score is held below full because the container change is durable in the wrong direction on one path: _prepare_section_context would raise at runtime the first time a source carries candidates, so the merged result is not safe until that consumer is repointed.
justifications.evidence: Strong for the new units and weak across the integration. tests/ids/test_candidate_persistence.py adds TestReadCandidates, TestSelectCandidates and TestCandidateRecordsStrict covering section derivation, Jev ordering, the two-IDS pick, the missing-edge refusal and the strict arms lookup; a live @pytest.mark.graph round-trip (test_read_and_select_candidates_round_trip) asserts the two-IDS marking and the route transition to selected; the declared negative control is genuine (tests/ids/test_candidates.py::test_gather_ids_context_reads_candidates_from_edges reddens with retrieve_candidates reinstated, negative_control.log:1 failed, EXIT=1). The gap is that no test drives _prepare_section_context, the live consumer of the changed value, so a green gate (530 passed) coexists with a reproducible AttributeError on that path (see findings). The gate reproduced here at base (524 passed, 8 skipped, 1 deselected, EXIT=0) and at head (530 passed, 8 skipped, 2 deselected, EXIT=0).
justifications.fit: The new functions sit beside their writer/eraser (write_candidates, count_candidates_by_route, clear_candidates) in imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py, matching the single-owner layout the section specifies; select_candidates is deliberately separate from write_candidates so a pick flags existing edges without rewriting the shortlist, and its docstring states that reason. Names are mechanism-based (read_candidates, select_candidates, section_id) with no plan label or attribution, and the discover importers delegate to the graph_ops reader as the plan directs.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's declared done-when items are all present: read_candidates and select_candidates live beside write_candidates in imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:576 and :636; gather_ids_context reads each source's shortlist from read_candidates (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:763) and no longer imports or calls retrieve_candidates (grep -n retrieve_candidates imas_codex/ids/mapping.py prints nothing); the imas_node_embedding arm and its post-hoc filter are gone from imas_codex/ids/tools.py (grep prints nothing); the route count is consolidated on graph_ops.py:788 with the workers.py copy and count_sources_by_mapping_status deleted (grep -rn 'def count_candidates_by_route' imas_codex/ prints only graph_ops.py:788) and discover status/clear repointed; _candidate_records raises CandidateWriteError on an unmatched judgment. But the change is not complete at the consumption end: gather_ids_context changed the type of each source's source_candidates entry from list[Candidate] to list[dict], and only one of the two consumers was updated. _prepare_section_context (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py:1225-1233) still reads cand.hit.path / cand.hit.score, the shape the removed retrieve_candidates returned; this is the consumer the live map worker takes.
justifications.reuse: No capability is forked. read_candidates replaces the per-IDS re-embedding retrieve_candidates call in gather_ids_context with a single MAPPING_CANDIDATE read; the route count collapses to one definition in graph_ops.py used by imas map status and discover status/clear; the removed imas_node_embedding arm deleted code whose hits were already discarded rather than adding a second bridge.
justifications.scope_discipline: The change stays inside the node's declared write paths for every source file it names: imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py, imas_codex/ids/mapping.py, imas_codex/ids/tools.py, imas_codex/ids/workers.py, imas_codex/cli/discover/__init__.py and tests under tests/ids, tests/cli and tests/tools. The next node's retired fields are correctly left untouched (mapping_target_ids remains in workers.py:243-245,299, owned by map-run-maps-each-home). One path sits outside the plan's node write paths: docs/evidence/fragments/mapping-candidate-selection/map-context-reads-candidates.html, a landing-evidence artifact the node declared in its orientation_write_paths; accepted.
